question.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x+1} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \,\text{d}x=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)\cdot x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)-\int \frac{x}{x+1}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use a substitution $x+1=u,$ thus $x=u-1$ and $\text{d}x=\text{d}u.$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)-\int \frac{x}{x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)-\int \frac{u-1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)-\int \,\text{d}u+\int \frac{\text{d}u}{u} \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)-u+\operatorname{ln}⁡u+D \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)-(x+1)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+D \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)-x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=D-1$ is an integral constant.
